newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair won't rule out privatisations.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair won't rule out privatisations.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour leader Tony Blair on Monday refused to rule out privatisations if his party wins the election called for May 1.
"There is no list of things that we are saying we are going to privatise but I look at these things on their own merits," he told BBC Television.
"It depends whether it is in the public interest to do it. I don't take an ideological view of this," he said.
Blair refused to be specific on budget plans should his party win power.
"I am not writing budgets five years in advance - or even a year in advance," he said.
"We cannot put 18 years right in 18 days," he said.
"Of course resources are important but they have left us with a huge hole in the public finances. They have doubled the national debt.
"We are keeping to the Conservatives' spending restrictions, not out of recognition of their superlative performance but out of recognition of their incompetence."
He insisted there were sharp differences between the Labour Party of old and the New Labour he has moulded.
"The idea that because it is not the old tax and spend' left and that therefore we don't offer anything new and different -- that is absurd," he said.
